        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>

This role is suited for someone with a strong academic or practical background in computer vision, AI, robotics, or perception systems. A Master’s degree is expected; a PhD is a strong plus. Your Mission

You will develop the vision and AI pipeline that turns raw camera data into actionable perception outputs for autonomous flight. Job Location Type: Remote

Job Description Summary

As a Remote Project Manager, you'll own the project management and implementation process for GE HealthCare Patient Care Solutions products including Monitoring Solutions within the Dallas market . This position includes, but is not limited to, sales order review, project planning and documentation, resource coordination, and issues resolution.

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description

Responsibilities

Working primarily from a home based office location from Texas (Dallas-Fort Worth is preferred), Oklahoma, or Kansas, the Remote Project Manager is responsible for driving customer satisfaction and process productivity throughout the project installation by:

  • Acting as the primary liaison between GE and customer project teams with onsite support from Service & Sales.
  • Identify GE and customer responsibilities and deliverables as defined in the sales contract.
  • Creation, maintenance, and routing of formal project implementation timeline with collaboration between the customer, GE HealthCare, and contract resources.
  • Maintaining accurate project milestone date accuracy creating visible and predictable project data for key business metrics and revenue forecasting.
  • Regular tracking and communication of implementation progress including project kick-off, regular status updates, and project closure. This includes tracking of equipment delivery, installation, and testing.
  • Identification, escalation and resolution of issues, which might affect customer satisfaction and GE operational targets.
  • Lead implementation team during clinical “GoLive” of the equipment.
  • Participation in process improvement initiatives.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelors degree and at least 2 years of project management experience, or an Associates degree and at least 5 years of Project Management experience.
  • Minimum 2 years of experience leading cross-functional teams.

Desired Characteristics

  • Demonstrate experience communicating effectively and facilitate meetings via teleconference or in person with multi-functional groups.
  • Experience managing multiple concurrent projects and competing priorities to meet scheduled project completion dates and customer expectations.
  • Demonstrate communicating with diverse work partners internal and external to GE and our customers.
  • Experience communicating complex technical issues in a customer-friendly manner.
  • Experience with large-scale project management where deadlines are met on or ahead of schedule; construction, healthcare IT or equipment installations experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated customer service experience working remotely with external customers in a clinical environment.
  • Formal coursework in project management and/or current Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
  • Knowledge/experience with the healthcare industry and GEHC products.
  • Willingness to travel up to 10%, with overnight stays when needed.
  • Ability to meet customer’s vendor credentialing requirements.

We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors, to act with humility and build trust, lead with transparency, deliver with focus, and drive ownership - always unyielding integrity.


Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

Akuna Capital is an innovative trading firm with a strong focus on collaboration, cutting-edge technology, data driven solutions, and automation. We specialize in providing liquidity as an options market maker – meaning we are committed to providing competitive quotes that we are willing to both buy and sell. To do this successfully, we design and implement our own low latency technologies, trading strategies, and mathematical models.

Our Founding Partnersfirst conceptualized Akuna in their hometown of Sydney. They opened the firm’s first office in 2011 in the heart of the derivatives industry and the options capital of the world – Chicago. Today, Akuna is proud to operate from additional offices in Sydney, Shanghai, London, and Singapore.

What you’ll do as a Platform Engineer at Akuna:

This is an exciting role where you will be given the opportunity to take ownership of projects and make them your own. At Akuna, we are constantly looking for ways to improve our efficiency as we continue to grow. As a Platform Engineer, you will work closely with our Trading, Development, Infrastructure, and Operations teams. You will design and implement cloud solutions, automate infrastructure as code, improve cloud governance and security, and monitor our hybrid-cloud environments. In this role, you will:

  • Ensure cloud services are leveraged to their full potential (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and best practices are being followed
  • Help manage our public cloud growth and continuously improve Akuna’s hybrid-cloud operating model
  • Evaluate proposed solution architectures and provide recommendations
  • Provision, configure, upgrade, and monitor technologies such as Kubernetes (EKS and on-premise), Spark, Kafka, and other large-scale distributed databases
  • Automate infrastructure management and development pipelines with tools like Terraform, Ansible, Jenkins and GitLab
  • Explore new technologies in the cloud-native/container ecosystem
  • Work with Infrastructure and Development teams to monitor systems, clusters and cloud deployments to detect errors and monitor performance
  • Adhere to the engineering mindset of creating and maintaining performant and reliable production systems

Qualities that make great candidates:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
  • 3+ years of experience in Platform Engineering, Cloud Engineering, SRE, DevOps, or related infrastructure roles
  • This role is available hybrid from our Chicago office or fully remote.
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect certification preferred
  • Deep experience deploying, operating, and scaling Kubernetes in production, including on-premise clusters and Amazon EKS
  • Strong expertise designing and managing cloud infrastructure on AWS; experience with GCP is a plus
  • Advanced proficiency with Terraform and Infrastructure as Code (IaC), including reusable module development, state management, and platform automation
  • Experience building and operating highly available, scalable, and secure cloud-native platforms
  • Strong knowledge of observability, including monitoring, logging, alerting, and operational troubleshooting
  • Proven experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines and modern software delivery practices
  • Strong Linux systems administration and troubleshooting skills in distributed production environments
  • Proficiency in automation and scripting with Python, Bash, or similar languages
  • Experience with cloud-native data services, including Amazon RDS, Aurora, Redshift, and DynamoDB
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives, influence architectural decisions, and mentor engineers
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with experience partnering across engineering, operations, and business teams
  • The ability to react quickly and accurately to rapidly changing market conditions, including the ability to quickly and accurately respond and/or solve math and coding problems are essential functions of the role

In addition to technical skillsets, Akuna values the unique perspectives people can bring to the table to collaboratively solve complex problems and drive Akuna forward. We want everyone to feel empowered to apply. We welcome your application and encourage you to take the first steps toward your future with us!

Please note that level/title will be determined upon the conclusion of the interview process. If you are a current student or recent graduate, please take a look at our Entry Level and Intern positions.

Please note that all final round interviews are conducted onsite at our Chicago office.

In accordance with Illinois Equal Pay Act, the minimum base salary starts at $145,000. Exact compensation offered may vary based on many factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and skill set. This role is also eligible for a discretionary performance bonus as part of the total compensation package and includes a comprehensive benefits package that may encompass employer-paid medical, dental, vision, retirement contributions, paid time off, and other benefits. The minimum base salary herein was determined in good faith by Akuna Capital LLC.

About Laurel Employment Law

We are not your traditional law firm. Laurel Employment Law is a fully remote, tech-driven plaintiff's firm that's redefining how employment law is practiced. We're a team of smart, ambitious litigators who collaborate to deliver outstanding results for our clients — and we have fun doing it! We use cutting-edge legal tech to eliminate inefficiencies, empower autonomy, and give our attorneys the freedom to focus on what matters: winning for our clients and building meaningful careers. If you thrive in a high-performance, growth-oriented culture and want to do your best work without commuting, micromanagement, or outdated systems, this is the place for you.

The Role

    We're looking for a winner — an experienced Employment Litigation Attorney who's hungry to deliver results, grow quickly, and play a key role in a modern, remote law firm that's scaling quickly. You'll manage your own caseload, leveraging technology, strategy, and teamwork to deliver winning outcomes for employees who've been wronged. You will be judged by your results, not office politics. Join us, embrace The Laurel Way, and you will win like never before.

The Culture

    Laurel is built differently. We started the Firm asking an important question, "what if it didn't have to suck to work at a law firm? In fact, what if it could be kind of awesome?" The result is an award-winning culture where we take the work seriously without ever taking ourselves too seriously. We've built a team of winners who work together to get more done, more efficiently, while leaving opposing counsel asking themselves, "how the heck did they do that?" We win and we have fun doing it. It's a better way to practice.

The Laurel Way

    Laurel is built on a foundation of 3 unique competitive advantages: Technology, Culture, and a Shared Services model that relieves you of the most arduous parts of the job. Imagine having fully drafted demand letters, complaints, discovery requests, discovery responses, and depo notices available to you at a click of a button produced at near-instantaneous speed. Our attorneys get more done, in less time, with far less aggravation. That means more time back in your day to be used in a high-impact way while putting the joy back into your practice of law.

What You'll Do

    • Own your cases from start to finish in a supportive, fully remote environment.

    • Draft pleadings, discovery, motions, and mediation briefs using our cloud-based systems.

    • Argue motions, take and defend depositions, and prepare for trial.

    • Drive strategy and make key case decisions with autonomy and impact.

    • Use our integrated tech tools to communicate, collaborate, and track performance.

    • Negotiate powerfully to achieve life-changing results for our clients.

    • Deliver a five-star client experience every time — we care as much as we fight.

    • Provide opportunities for mentorship to junior attorneys as they grow their practice.

Your Skills & Mindset

    • Licensed and in good standing with the California State Bar.

    • 5+ years of experience in California employment litigation.

    • Superb research, writing, and analytical ability.

    • Creative, strategic thinker who thrives in a remote-first, tech-savvy team.

    • Able to manage a large caseload while staying organized and proactive.

    • Motivated, ambitious, radically optimistic and driven to grow your income and your career.

Why Laurel

    • Fully Remote — work from anywhere in California with world-class collaboration tools.

    • Tech-Enabled Efficiency — we use automation, dashboards, and smart systems so you can focus on lawyering, not admin.

    • Culture That Wins Together — no egos, no bureaucracy — just sharp, driven people who push and support each other.

    • Uncapped Compensation Potential — base range $186k – $220k plus uncapped bonuses based on performance

    • Paid time off, holidays, health insurance, referral bonuses, and real opportunities for advancement.

Come Shape the Future

    If you want to practice law at the highest level — remotely, intelligently, and collaboratively — come build with us. Laurel Employment Law is where talented attorneys thrive, grow, and win.

Senior Account Executive - Life Sciences (US, Remote)

➡️ Frustrated selling a product that's difficult to differentiate or competing purely on price?

➡️ Want to represent an AI platform trusted by Pfizer, Moderna, Roche, GSK and thousands of other innovation-led organisations?

If this sounds like your next move, we’d love to hear from you.

Role Summary:

The Life Sciences industry is changing rapidly, and AI is becoming central to how the world's leading pharmaceutical and biotech companies innovate. At Patsnap, we're at the heart of that transformation.

We're looking for a Senior Account Executive to help accelerate one of our fastest-growing business units. With 20%+ year-on-year growth, significant investment in AI, and ambitious expansion plans, there's never been a more exciting time to join our Life Sciences team.

This isn't about selling another point solution.

You'll represent one of the most comprehensive AI-powered Innovation Intelligence platforms on the market, bringing together patents, scientific literature, clinical trials, regulatory intelligence, market data and proprietary AI to help customers make smarter R&D and IP decisions.

Trusted by organisations including Pfizer, Moderna, Roche, Novartis, GSK, Bayer, Sanofi and Johnson & Johnson, you'll partner with global pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device companies to solve some of their most important innovation challenges—from accelerating drug discovery to reducing R&D risk and shaping long-term innovation strategy.

You'll own strategic enterprise opportunities from prospecting through to close, engaging senior stakeholders across R&D, Innovation, Intellectual Property and the C-suite. These are commercially significant, multi-stakeholder sales cycles where you'll build trusted relationships, influence complex buying decisions and deliver measurable business value.

If you're looking for a role where you can sell a genuinely differentiated product, own a strategic territory, and play a key role in one of Patsnap's highest-growth markets, we'd love to hear from you.

Want to see the platform you'd be representing?

Check out this short overview:

This is a remote US-based position, ideally suited for candidates able to work flexibly across EST hours.

Who are we?

Patsnap is a global, pre-IPO company that transforms the way organizations harness their Intellectual Property and Research & Development productivity. Our platform revolutionizes how IP and R&D teams collaborate across the entire innovation lifecycle, using domain-specific AI to accelerate the creation of market-ready products. With over 12,000 customers worldwide, including some of the biggest names in innovation, Patsnap is at the forefront of technological advancement. Our $300M Series E funding round brings our valuation to a $1 billion unicorn status, and we still have a remarkable amount of growth ahead.

As the leading global Life Sciences intelligence platform, Patsnap helps pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, and life sciences organisations make better innovation decisions. By connecting patents, scientific literature, clinical trials, regulatory data, and market intelligence, we enable our customers to identify white spaces, reduce R&D risk, and accelerate breakthrough innovation.

We have a vibrant and diverse team with offices in Singapore, Toronto, London, Shanghai and remote teams based in US. Our hyper-growth trajectory is powered by our people, and we are extremely proud of our company-wide vision, work ethic, and entrepreneurial spirit. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where talent thrives and ideas bloom.

Why Join Patsnap?

  • Sell a platform customers genuinely want to buy. Trusted by leading Life Sciences organisations including Pfizer, Moderna, Roche, Novartis, GSK, Bayer, Sanofi and Johnson & Johnson, Patsnap helps customers solve mission-critical R&D and innovation challenges.

  • Join one of our fastest-growing business units. With 20%+ year-on-year growth, significant investment in AI, and ambitious expansion plans, there's never been a more exciting time to join our Life Sciences team.

  • Own a high-value territory with real opportunity. Take ownership of strategic enterprise accounts, combining new business with significant expansion potential across pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device organisations.

  • Sell a genuinely differentiated solution. Patsnap brings together AI, patents, scientific literature, clinical trials, regulatory intelligence and market data in one platform, helping customers make smarter innovation and R&D decisions.

  • Have conversations that matter. Partner with senior stakeholders across R&D, Innovation, Intellectual Property and Commercial leadership, influencing decisions that shape future products, portfolios and scientific breakthroughs.

  • Join a high-performance commercial team. Work alongside experienced sales leaders in a collaborative culture that values curiosity, ownership, continuous learning and shared success.

  • Accelerate your career. As Patsnap continues to invest in Life Sciences globally, you'll have the opportunity to grow into strategic account leadership, larger enterprise opportunities, or broader commercial leadership roles.

  • Build and execute a territory strategy to drive new logo acquisition across pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical device organisations.

  • Develop executive relationships across R&D, Innovation, Intellectual Property and Commercial leadership teams.

  • Lead complex, multi-stakeholder sales processes, creating consensus across technical and commercial buyers.

  • Build, manage and accurately forecast a healthy pipeline of enterprise opportunities.

  • Partner closely with SDRs, Customer Success, Product and Marketing to maximise territory growth.

  • Consistently achieve and exceed revenue targets while contributing to the continued growth of the Life Sciences business.

  • Experience selling into Life Sciences organisations, including pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device or adjacent markets.

  • Confident in high-volume outbound outreach; from cold calling to pipeline building and engaging prospects.

  • Confidence managing complex, consultative enterprise sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders.

  • Experience engaging senior decision-makers and executive buyers.

  • Strong commercial acumen with the ability to translate technical capabilities into business value.

  • A proactive, self-motivated approach with experience building pipeline alongside inbound opportunities.

  • Excellent communication, presentation and negotiation skills.

  • A growth mindset, intellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in AI, innovation and Life Sciences.

A genuinely strong sales culture we’re really proud of. High-performing but low ego, social, and dynamic. It’s a team that supports each other, shares best practice, raises standards, and celebrates wins properly together. Alongside a great product, it’s one of the best parts of working here.

  • Degree, certification, or formal training in nursing, medical assisting, or another healthcare field.
  • Experience supporting psychiatric, behavioral health, telehealth, primary care, or specialty medical providers.
  • Familiarity with psychiatric medication terminology and medication-management processes.
  • Experience supporting physicians, nurse practitioners, or other prescribing providers.
  • Experience reviewing clinical documentation for prior authorization submissions.
  • Experience handling insurance denials, appeals, and follow-up.
  • Knowledge of gender-affirming care and LGBTQIA+ healthcare needs.
  • Experience with insurance verification, referrals, claims communication, or healthcare compliance.
  • Experience using Tebra, IntakeQ, Spruce, CoverMyMeds, or comparable platforms.

  • Experience creating SOPs or improving administrative workflows.
  • Project coordination or healthcare operations management experience.

  • Full-time role

  • 100% remote position

  • Opportunity to work in an inclusive, mission-driven mental health setting

  • Exposure to modern digital health platforms and patient communication tools

  • Collaborative, supportive work culture with space to grow professionally

    About Ume Intelligence

    Ume Intelligence is a marketing science company solving complex commercial problems for multi-location restaurant brands. We build modern analytics and automation infrastructure, paired with hands-on digital operations that turn operational data into measurable revenue.

    We operate as a lean, high-leverage team with no walls between engineering and operations. We look for people who run toward technology, automation, and data models rather than away from them—and who evaluate success by real business impact (margin, demand, and net revenue) rather than vanity metrics or features shipped.

    The Role

    We are looking for a Forward-Deployed Product Manager to sit at the center of how Ume works: bridging our clients, our forward-deployed marketers, our founders, and our engineering team.

    A restaurant brand’s demand comes from search, delivery marketplaces, its own customer database, and foot traffic past the door. These levers interact dynamically, yet restaurant operators lack the time to model any of it. You will own the software workflows that model these interactions and the operational mechanics that run on them every day.

    When an operational edge case occurs for a client, you resolve it immediately and engineer safeguards so it cannot happen again. When an operator executes the same workflow manually for the third time, you convert it into a structured process, an automated check, or a software spec, and partner with engineering to build it.

    This role starts with high-context individual ownership across product definition and client operations. As our deployment expands, the position is designed to transition into leading and scaling the team.

    What You’ll Own

    • Client operations, end to end. Take complete ownership of client operational data (menus, pricing architectures, localized promotions, search listings, and CRM segments across delivery aggregators). Maintain zero tolerance for client-facing discrepancies.

    • Fix it, then prevent it. Catch issues before clients do. Trace each one to its cause and close the loop with a process change, an automated check, or a product fix, so the same problem does not come back.

    • Product Discovery and Specifications: Synthesize feedback directly from brand operators, growth marketers, and company founders into structured product specifications. Validate and accept engineering releases, measuring whether features moved targeted operational or commercial metrics.

    • Commercial and Unit Economics: Rigorously model client-level channel economics (net margins after commissions, ad discounts, and delivery fees) alongside internal unit economics (internal cost-to-serve per client account).

    • The Technical-Commercial Bridge: Partner daily with software engineers, forward-deployed marketers, and company leadership, spending dedicated hours each week directly with brand executives. Translate ambiguous business problems into crisp technical requirements and explain technical capabilities in terms of commercial lift.

    • Concurrent Program Delivery: Drive multiple client implementations, product features, and operational priorities in parallel without dropping critical details. Maintain clarity on which priority moves the needle each day.

    • Team and System Scalability: Design the operating cadences, playbooks, and onboarding standards as the company grows, helping evaluate, hire, and train future team members.

    Your First 90 Days

    1. Day 30. You own day-to-day operations for at least one enterprise client account and have documented an end-to-end demand and margin map identifying key points of failure.

    2. Day 60. You have specified and shipped at least one software improvement with clear commercial or operational metrics attached.

    3. Day 90. You have eliminated a recurring class of client operational issues through an automated check or productized feature.

    What You Bring

    Experience & Background

    • Around 4+ years in product management, product operations, forward-deployed engineering/ops, or a high-rigor analytics/consulting role where you owned measurable outcomes rather than slide recommendations. Tenure is a benchmark, not a rigid constraint; demonstrated execution takes precedence.

    • Demonstrated experience working directly alongside engineering teams in a software company, venture-backed startup, digital agency or technical consulting environment.

    • Relevant academic grounding (Engineering, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or Business). An MBA or advanced degree from a premier global program (e.g., IIMs, ISB, INSEAD, or reputed US/European/Asian business schools) is a strong advantage, though demonstrated judgment and execution track record remain the primary evaluation criteria.

    Core Competencies & Must-Haves

    • Detail-Oriented: You spot the misconfigured price tier, the missing inventory item, and the conflicting campaign dates. You audit your own work before external stakeholders see it.

    • Business-Savvy: You understand multi-unit retail economics and know how marketing, localized pricing, and aggregator commissions interact with store P&Ls.

    • Technical Acumen: You are comfortable working with structured data schemas, spreadsheets, SQL-level data logic, platform APIs, and modern developer toolchains. You can debate technical trade-offs with engineers without needing to write production code.

    • Systems Thinking: You naturally look for recurring patterns and architectural solutions rather than settling for repetitive manual interventions.

    • Multi-Threading: You manage multiple concurrent operational threads cleanly, maintaining strict organization, proactive documentation, and clear stakeholder communication.

    • Leadership & Trust: You build rapid credibility with engineering leads, commercial marketers, and enterprise clients, demonstrating the ability to drive alignment without formal authority.

    • Executive Communication: Crisp, articulate written and spoken English. Much of our work is delivered through specifications, memos, and client updates, with frequent presentations directly to executive brand leadership.

    Nice to Have

    • Domain background in restaurants, food & beverage networks, or multi-location retail brands.

    • Hands-on familiarity with third-party delivery marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub), local search/SEO ecosystems, or retention CRM architectures.

    • Experience with restaurant POS ecosystems, dynamic pricing engines, or revenue management systems.

    • Daily utilization of modern AI workflows (prompt frameworks, local automation scripts, LLM interfaces) to accelerate operational velocity.

    • Experience hiring, onboarding, or mentoring technical operators or junior product managers.

    Working Hours

    • Full-time schedule with flexibility outside core touchpoints.

    • We expect dedicated collaboration hours with US clients and our forward-deployed marketers, typically between 6:00 AM and 12:00 PM US Pacific Time.

    How Performance Is Measured

    You will operate with modern automation tools, analytics infrastructure, and engineering resources. With that leverage comes a clear standard for analytical rigor, client impact, and operational discipline:

    • Execution Precision & Quality Assurance (35% Weight):
      In multi-location brand operations, accuracy across pricing, menu configurations, and campaign setups directly protects client margin and trust.
      Target: Zero high-severity client-facing defects on live accounts; 100% adherence to pre-launch validation workflows.

    • Product Impact & Workflow Leverage (30% Weight):
      Converting real operational friction into software specifications that remove bottlenecks and expand team throughput.
      Target: Identified problems successfully specified, accepted by engineering, and deployed; measurable reduction in manual operational time across client accounts.

    • Commercial Economics & Account Health (20% Weight):
      Measurable commercial improvements across client channels and internal cost-to-serve metrics.
      Target: Progress against client-specific net margin targets and proactive containment of account service costs.

    • Stakeholder Leadership & Dependability (15% Weight):
      Cross-functional trust with software engineers, marketing operators, and client leadership during core US collaboration windows.
      Target: Consistent schedule reliability during US Pacific overlap hours, proactive stakeholder communication, and high ratings across client and internal reviews.

    What We Offer

    • Competitive Full-Time Compensation: Stable, competitive monthly base salary benchmarked for high-performing talent.

    • Meaningful Equity Participation: Opportunity to earn stock options and hold real equity upside in a venture-backed, high-growth US company as we scale.

    • Paid Time Off & Holidays: Generous paid annual leave plus observed corporate holidays.

    • A Path to Lead: Direct path to expand the forward-deployed product function and step into team leadership as organizational headcount grows.

    • High Leverage, Low Bureaucracy: Direct exposure to founders, clients, and core architecture in an environment with minimal meetings and zero political bloat.

    At Talkspace, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and belonging-centered workplace where everyone can thrive while making a difference in mental health. Want to help over two million people receive quality mental healthcare? Come join our mission to get therapy into the hands of everyone!

    We’re looking for a part-time, contract Therapist (Independent Contract Provider) who is passionate about reaching individuals who need mental healthcare but lack easy access to it. This role is perfect for those seeking the opportunity to work with a diverse client base while enjoying the flexibility and rewards of private practice—without the hassle of administrative work. Let Talkspace handle the insurance billing, marketing, and administrative costs, so you can create your own schedule and focus fully on providing impactful care!

    What you'll do:

    • Treat clients remotely in your state(s) of licensure on the secure (HIPAA compliant) Talkspace platform
    • Conduct client sessions using video, audio, and live messaging services
    • Respond to asynchronous client messages each week, in a timely manner
    • Complete your required clinical documentation after each client session

    About you

    • Current license to practice independently without supervision in the state of Ohio
      • Licensed Independent Social Worker (LISW)
      • Licensed Independent Social Worker - Supervisor (LISW-S)
      • Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT)
      • Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor (LPCC)
      • Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor - Supervisor (LPCC-S)
    • Individual professional malpractice liability insurance policy
    • Individual NPI number
    • Comfortable learning new online tools and technology
    • Reliable internet connection and video-capable device

    Perks

    • Clients Ready for You: Talkspace provides new client referrals
    • Flexible Schedule: Set your own schedule with no minimum requirement for your weekly hours or caseload size
    • No Membership Fees: No provider fees
    • Accept Insurance Without Hassle: Talkspace will take care of all aspects of client insurance including credentialing, billing, and claims
    • Everything in One Place: Sessions, clinical documentation, resources, and compensation tracking on one platform

    • Free CEUs: NBCC and ASWB accredited continuing education credits via Talkspace-provided Learning Communities
    • Health Perks: Access Stride Health to support your health and financial well-being

    Compensation

    • $70 per hour for live chat, audio, or video sessions (this rate is prorated for 45 and 30 minute sessions)
    • Additional compensation for asynchronous messaging
    • Earn a new client engagement bonus, varying by plan type

    Please note: If you treat clients in multiple states, different rates will apply accordingly. Rates could be subject to change and may vary over time based on the market and shifts in demand.

    Why Talkspace

    Talkspace is a leading virtual behavioral healthcare provider committed to helping people lead healthier, happier lives through access to high-quality mental healthcare. At Talkspace, we believe that mental healthcare is core to overall health and should be available to everyone.

    Talkspace pioneered the ability to text with a licensed therapist from anywhere and now offers a comprehensive suite of mental health services, including therapy for individuals, teens, and couples, as well as psychiatric treatment and medication management (18+). With Talkspace’s core therapy offerings, members are matched with one of thousands of licensed therapists within days and can engage in live video, audio, or chat sessions, and/or unlimited asynchronous text messaging sessions.

    All care offered at Talkspace is delivered through an easy-to-use, fully-encrypted web and mobile platform that meets HIPAA, federal, and state regulatory requirements. More than 151 million Americans have access to Talkspace through their health insurance plans, employee assistance programs, our partnerships with leading healthcare companies, or as a free benefit through their employer, school, or government agency.

    EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

    Talkspace welcomes and celebrates talent from all backgrounds, perspectives, and walks of life to foster an innovative and diverse workforce. We encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification or if your path has been nontraditional — such as not completing a formal degree program, taking a career break, or having a prior criminal record — if you believe you could make a great addition to this team. Come as you are and learn about the exciting opportunities on our team.

    Individuals seeking employment at Talkspace are considered without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, national origin, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, marital, parental, veteran or military status, unfavorable military discharge, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

    How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

    Diversity

    Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

    Equity

    Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

    Inclusion

    Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

    Belonging

    Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

    About No deviation

    At No deviation, we are dedicated to delivering patient-centric solutions that revolutionize the pharmaceutical landscape. As a dynamic expert in engineering consultancy, Commissioning Qualification Validation (CQV), and Quality, Compliance, and Regulatory services, we are looking for individuals who are excited to contribute to impactful projects and drive innovation.

    We believe that great things happen when Empathy, Integrity, and Transparency guide our actions. That's why we foster a culture of collaboration, inclusion, and continuous development – empowering our team members to grow personally and professionally.

    Position Overview

    We are seeking an experienced IT/OT Project Lead to lead the assessment, planning, and implementation readiness for a site-wide upgrade of OT computerized systems to Windows 11 LTSC. The environment includes approximately 70+ GMP and non-GMP OT system assets distributed across Manufacturing, QC Laboratories, and Development Laboratories. The role will initially focus on conducting a comprehensive current-state assessment and developing a detailed, phased project roadmap covering technical feasibility, system dependencies, resource requirements, cost estimates, timelines, risks, procurement requirements, and implementation strategy. The successful candidate should have sufficient technical understanding of OT infrastructure, computerized systems, and regulated manufacturing environments to effectively engage with Engineering, Manufacturing, QC, IT/OT, Quality, vendors, and system integrators.

    Key Responsibilities

    • Lead a comprehensive assessment of the current OT computerized system landscape, including Windows OS versions, hardware, applications, interfaces, and dependencies.
    • Develop an inventory and categorisation of approximately 70+ GMP and non-GMP OT systems across Manufacturing, QC, and Development Labs.
    • Assess system readiness and compatibility for migration to Windows 11 LTSC.
    • Identify technical gaps, obsolescence risks, cybersecurity concerns, dependencies, and upgrade constraints.
    • Engage equipment vendors, application vendors, and system integrators to confirm Windows 11 compatibility, hardware requirements, software/application upgrade requirements, licensing requirements, and vendor support requirements.
    • Define a risk-based and phased upgrade strategy for the site.
    • Develop the overall project plan, including scope, WBS, schedule and milestones, cost estimates, resource requirements, procurement requirements, vendor support, and risk management.
    • Develop business case and budgetary estimates for project approval.
    • Define implementation sequencing to minimise impact to manufacturing and laboratory operations.
    • Develop the proposed approach for testing, commissioning, system verification/qualification, cutover, rollback, and operational handover.
    • Coordinate stakeholders across Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, QC, Development Labs, IT/OT, Quality, and vendors.
    • Establish project governance, risk tracking, and management reporting.
    • Support vendor selection, technical evaluation, and tender/RFP activities where required.
    • Prepare the project for transition from assessment and planning into execution.

    Required Qualifications

    • Degree in Engineering, Information Technology, Automation, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
    • Strong project management experience involving OT systems, industrial IT infrastructure, or computerized systems.
    • Experience managing operating system migration / infrastructure upgrade / technology refresh projects highly preferred.
    • Good understanding of Windows operating systems, OT infrastructure, industrial computerized systems, network and system dependencies, and cybersecurity considerations.
    • Experience within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other regulated manufacturing environments strongly preferred.
    • Ability to work across both technical and business stakeholders.
    • Strong project planning, cost estimation, risk management, and stakeholder management capabilities.
    • Experience coordinating equipment vendors, software vendors, and system integrators.
    • Familiarity with project planning tools such as Microsoft Project, Primavera, or equivalent.

    Why join us?

    • Generous Leave Policy.
    • Comprehensive Health & Wellness Coverage: Receive robust medical and dental coverage to support your health needs.
    • Professional Development Opportunities: Access continuous learning programs and resources for career growth within the company.
    • Inclusive Culture: Work in an environment where innovation, collaboration, and diverse perspectives are encouraged and celebrated.
    • Shape the Future: Make a real difference in the pharmaceutical industry while advancing your career.

    How to apply

    Are you ready to play a key role in shaping the future of pharmaceutical solutions? If you're passionate about making an impact, we want you on our team!

    Please submit your resume, outlining your qualifications and experience relevant to the role, here.

      <title>ZoomInfo Technologies LLC: Director, Applied AI</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Bethesda, Maryland, United States; Remote-US-MA; Remote-US-MD; Remote-US-WA; Vancouver, Washington, United States; Waltham, Massachusetts, United States
</p>

<div class="content-intro"><p>ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen–fast.</p></div><div>
<p class="markdown-p">You'll lead the team that builds the intelligence every ZoomInfo AI agent reasons over — what's true about companies and the people in them, how they relate, and what they're buying. This role owns the B2B data graph strategy end to end, blending classical machine learning and data science with LLM and agentic systems, and treating evaluation and inference cost as core disciplines. You'll set the technical bar for a team of senior engineers while staying close to the code, shipping alongside the people you lead.</p>
<p class="markdown-p"><strong class="markdown-strong">What You'll Do</strong></p>
<ul class="markdown-ul">
<li class="markdown-li">You will ship code alongside your team, prototype alone to prove or kill an idea, and review code as a peer, setting how the team uses agentic coding tools with precise specifications and rigorous review.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will own delivery end-to-end, from problem framing through serving and on-call, including long-tail graph coverage and user memory for agents that separates user-supplied context from system-of-record data.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will choose the right method for each problem — classical machine learning, language models, or code — for challenges like sparse-company revenue estimation, entity resolution, and semantic intent modeling, deciding on measured evidence and stopping work that won't pay off.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will define what it takes to claim an agent's output is correct, not just that its run completed, building the evaluation datasets, regression gates, and experiment designs that back those claims.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will own inference cost, latency, and capacity, including build-versus-buy and distillation decisions, since a model too expensive to run everywhere isn't a result.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will hire and grow machine learning engineers, data scientists, and research engineers, developing senior engineers into technical leaders.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will work across product, platform, security, and legal, and present results and their limits to executives, including when a system isn't good enough to launch.</li>
</ul>
<p class="markdown-p"><strong class="markdown-strong">What You Bring</strong></p>
<p class="markdown-p"><em class="markdown-em">Must-Have:</em></p>
<ul class="markdown-ul">
<li class="markdown-li">You have significant experience building production machine learning systems and leading the engineers who build them by shipping alongside them — demonstrated capability matters more than years.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have a track record of hiring and developing senior machine learning engineers and data scientists against a high bar.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You stay hands-on today: shipping code, building prototypes independently, and using agentic coding tools daily with rigorous review.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You bring deep classical machine learning and data science expertise (supervised learning, feature engineering, statistical inference and experiment design, strong SQL) alongside production LLM and agentic systems, with the judgment to choose between them, including setting an evaluation bar with leakage-safe validation, calibration, and validated LLM judges.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have a record of cost and capacity decisions for model serving, such as moving a workload from a hosted model to a distilled or self-hosted one, with the savings measured, and you report results to executives with their limits stated, including recommending against a launch.</li>
</ul>
<p class="markdown-p"><em class="markdown-em">Preferred:</em></p>
<ul class="markdown-ul">
<li class="markdown-li">You bring entrepreneurial experience — founding a company, or taking a product from inception to paying customers as a founding or early engineer.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have experience in propensity modeling, ranking and retrieval, clustering, or entity resolution at scale.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have worked on web-scale language processing over multilingual, noisy text, knowledge graphs, or user memory for agents.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have experience with post-training and distillation, open-weight model serving, or AI governance and safety practices (ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF).</li>
</ul>
<p class="markdown-p">&nbsp;</p>

<div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>Be Part of Building the Future</strong></h2>
<p>Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&amp;P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. <p>In this role you will get opportunities to implement and maintain CI/CD systems and developer productivity solutions. You will be responsible for both regularly scheduled work as well as on-demand break-fix work to support Dremio’s CI/CD system, identifying areas of improvement, and implementing changes to increase efficiency and effectiveness of those systems.</p>
<p>Bring your industry experience to improve the efficiency and scale of Dremio’s infrastructure via innovation on tooling and methodologies. You should have empathy for developers and a passion for engineering productivity.&nbsp;</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>What you’ll be doing</strong></p>
